evaluations.expect: A job and its completed file remain readable after API and worker replacement.
Overlapping API revisions share status, global active limit and stored-size admission counters.
Crash after job/outbox save but before task creation is repaired; ambiguous task-create response does not create duplicate logical jobs.
Concurrent delivery claims one active attempt; replay after completion acknowledges without conversion.
Killed worker is retried after lease expiry; stale completion cannot replace a newer result or change counters twice.
A failed attempt cannot publish a partial file; upload generation, size and winning attempt are verified before done.
Worker identity cannot read Firestore, list/read unrelated objects, access secrets, invoke unrelated services or modify final result objects.
Upload policy rejects another job/key and oversized content; all signed capabilities expire promptly.
A deck greater than 32 MiB and within 300 MB can upload and download without buffering the whole file in the API.
Queue exhaustion/dead delivery results in eventual failed state and one capacity release, never permanently active jobs.
Expiry blocks new downloads exactly at 24 hours; cleanup removes objects and reconciles counters, with bounded soft-delete/version retention.

Application/task logs omit tokens, source URLs, callback credentials and policies. Generated download signatures never appear in Cloud Run URLs; legacy query URLs are excluded from retained/exported request logs with an explicit ingestion limitation.
Existing local offline suites and real MCP SDK tests pass; three-tool and REST contracts remain compatible.
Public health and TLS pass; missing/wrong token is 401; valid token lists exact tools; known private-address conversion fails safely.
Deployed source link resolves to matching AGPL source with no credentials, private fixtures or local-only records.
Rollback uses compatible durable records, preserves completed files and never interrupts or modifies the existing AEO service.
Concurrent/repeated upload to the same attempt key is rejected; signer cannot write final prefix; stale capabilities cannot overwrite completed artifacts.
Crashes before/after promotion and before/after Firestore publication recover without deleting a referenced winner or leaking unaccounted objects.
Reservations count staging/final copies/retries/orphans; expiry/deletion and concurrent admission never double-release storage.
Delayed first delivery, parent death, native hung child, request cancellation and dispatch timeout cannot leave a reusable lease while an old conversion keeps running.
Status near expiry reports accurate remaining lifetime; direct Storage signed links expire no later than the job and cannot expose another object.
Effective Cloud Run/Storage/Tasks logging and all inherited sinks are inspected; no guarantee of pre-ingestion redaction is inferred from exclusion filters.
Worker capabilities cannot invoke maintenance, operate on another job, finish another attempt or substitute a coordinator URL.
HTTP/task lease conflicts do not exhaust the three claimed-conversion-attempt budget; a delayed delivery can recover before the absolute job deadline.
An upload held open before capability expiry and completed after cleanup cannot produce an unaccounted object; uncertain reservations remain charged until a proven terminal/fenced outcome.
links_expire_in matches the actual generation-pinned signed GET deadline; expires_at describes retention and cannot be extended by polling.
